thesis: Monolithic Power Systems supplies the analog and power-management silicon and modules that deliver electricity inside AI servers, GPUs, memory, optical modules, switches and cars, and its growth is accelerating rather than decelerating: revenue rose 26.4% in FY2025 to $2.79B, then 47.6% year over year in Q2 2026 to a record $980.6M, with Q3 2026 guided to ~$1.15B, roughly 16% above consensus at the time. The thesis is content per socket as MPS shifts from selling chips to selling encapsulated power modules, backed by $1.39B net cash, 31.7% ROIC and a newly announced GlobalFoundries 300mm Singapore capacity agreement that addresses the supply ceiling from early 2027. The offset is price: 82x trailing GAAP earnings, 42x forward and 65x EV/EBITDA against a semiconductor peer median near 17x EV/EBITDA, so an AI digestion cycle would compress the multiple faster than earnings could offset. Both published Street consensus targets ($1,731 and $1,840) sit 28-36% above spot.

drivers: AI rack power density keeps climbing and Enterprise Data holds the raised full-year pace set in Q2 2026 (segment up 45% sequentially)
GlobalFoundries 300mm Singapore capacity lands on schedule in early 2027, lifting the supply ceiling management has extended significantly beyond $6B
Module and full-solution mix keeps raising content per socket and non-GAAP operating margin above the 37.5% printed in Q2 2026
800V AC-to-DC data center power and DDR5 memory-interface controllers convert from sampling to revenue in 2027, opening new addressable content
Automotive ramp from 1,500-plus new sockets across zonal, 48V, battery management and LiDAR adds a second growth engine independent of AI capex
FY2027 non-GAAP EPS of $40-45 (author estimate) capitalised at 50-58x

base_case.assumptions: Revenue grows ~45% in 2026 and ~25% in 2027, gross margin holds near 55% by management choice, non-GAAP operating margin settles at 37-38%, and the forward multiple compresses modestly to 50-55x. Band straddles the two published consensus targets: $1,839.80 average from 17 analysts polled by S&P Global and $1,731.42 from the 15 brokerages tracked by MarketBeat.

risks: AI digestion cycle arrives before the Singapore capacity ships, leaving committed capex and rising inventory against plateauing Enterprise Data demand
Multiple resets from 42x forward toward 30x on flat-to-down earnings — at 82x trailing GAAP and 113x trailing FCF the valuation carries no support
China manufacturing concentration exposed to export controls, tariffs or retaliatory measures before the multi-partner supply strategy matures
Back-end module assembly and test capacity fails to scale with demand, by management's own description the harder half of the problem
Inventory turnover of 2.51x and 140 days of inventory unwind slowly in a demand air pocket
Lower bound approaches the 52-week low of $833.18; the lowest published Street target of $1,200 sits above this range

catalysts.event: Ex-dividend date for the Q3 2026 dividend of $2.00 per share, declared 10 September 2026 — eighth consecutive year of dividend growth
Q3 2026 results after market close — guided to ~$1.15B revenue at the midpoint versus $986.8M consensus at the time of guidance, roughly 56% year-over-year growth
Automotive production ramp from more than 1,500 new design-win sockets across zonal architectures, 48V systems, battery management and LiDAR
Q4 and full-year 2026 results with first framing of FY2027 — the test of whether ~45% 2026 growth extends or normalises

GlobalFoundries 300mm Singapore capacity comes online under the 9 September 2026 manufacturing partnership, deploying MPS proprietary process technology for automotive power, industrial robotics and AI smart power stages (financial terms undisclosed)
First revenue from 800V AC-to-DC data center power solutions and DDR5 memory-interface controllers, both currently sampling

key_risks: Valuation: 82x trailing GAAP earnings, 42x forward, 65x EV/EBITDA and 113x trailing free cash flow against a semiconductor peer median near 17x EV/EBITDA — a single in-line quarter can cost 20%
AI capex cyclicality: Enterprise Data and Communications drive the acceleration and both ride hyperscaler spending, so a 2027 digestion cycle would hit after capex is committed
China manufacturing concentration plus tariff, export-control and cross-strait risk; the GlobalFoundries Singapore diversification does not help until 2027
Back-end execution: module assembly and test capacity is harder to scale than wafers by management's own account, the most plausible path to a demand-rich year disappointing
Working capital: 140 days of inventory and 2.51x turnover, with trailing free cash flow down 17% to $585.5M as capex and working capital absorb cash
Competition from Texas Instruments, Analog Devices, Infineon, Renesas, onsemi, Vicor and Navitas in AI power delivery, vertical power and 800V conversion
Governance optics: roughly $723M of insider selling over the trailing year with no reported buying against 3.53% insider ownership, plus an explicit management decision to cap gross margin near 55%
Beta of 1.66 and a 52-week range of $833.18-$1,714.09 — a 106% peak-to-trough spread demands position sizing discipline
